_comment: Run template for synthetic-ahu-sensor-bias (generated by CAMBER, no real building): two identical air handlers on a fixed 55 F supply setpoint, one with a supply-air sensor reading 3 F high. supply_air_control (the trended SAT against its setpoint), supply_air_reset_compliance against the site's design reset (55 F at 70 F outdoors up to 62 F at 60 F: t_max 62, so the map is the site's, not the G36 default, and the gap is priced with the reheat capacity in report.rcx.loads) and leaking_valve (the supply air against the mixed air with both valves shut, allowing 2 F of fan heat). Measured: supply_air_control passes both units (the loop holds each reading at 55 F); supply_air_reset_compliance warns on both (below the site's target 54 % of the occupied hours, mean gap 3.06 F); leaking_valve faults on AHU__sat_bias only (86.5 % of the valve-shut samples more than 3 F beyond the fan heat; no valve leaks: its sensor reads 3 F high) and passes AHU__healthy. The LOGGER equipment (a duct logger's reading for four days) is not discovered by this template; report.rcx.references compares each unit's supply-air sensor with its logger in the RCx layout (0.108, #267): AHU__sat_bias's reads +3.0 F (warn), so its leaking_valve and reset findings become conditional and the reset estimate ($5,250/yr) is at risk, while AHU__healthy's compares clean (+0.0 F) and its identical reset finding ($5,230/yr) stays firm.
